name: TimescaleDB
model: Postgres extension: hypertables auto-partitioned by time, full SQL, continuous aggregates (auto-refreshed rollups)
engine_note: Postgres heap and B-tree indexes per time chunk; older chunks converted to a compressed columnstore (Hypercore) in the Community edition
consistency: Inherits Postgres: multi-row ACID transactions, read committed by default, serializable as an option, fsync on commit by default; streaming replicas can serve slightly stale reads.
scaling: Single Postgres node: bigger machine plus read replicas; compression and tiering cold chunks to object storage (Tiger Cloud). Multi-node sharding was removed in 2.14 (2024).
licence: Apache 2.0 for the core; Timescale License (TSL, source-available) for Community features such as columnstore and continuous aggregates

licence_events.event: Timescale introduces the Timescale License (TSL), source-available, for new features; it bars offering them as a hosted database service (exact day unconfirmed)
TSL updated to add 'right to repair' and 'right to improve'; the ban on offering it as a service stays (exact day unconfirmed)
Company Timescale renames itself Tiger Data (cloud becomes Tiger Cloud); the extension keeps the name TimescaleDB and its licences

reach: Reach for it when time-stamped data (events, metrics, IoT) needs SQL joins with your other Postgres tables, compression and rollups, at up to billions of rows per node.
avoid: Avoid when a cloud Postgres you must use only ships the Apache edition (no compression or continuous aggregates), or when data outgrows one node.
escape: Plain Postgres tables slow down on huge append-only time series; it adds time partitions, compression, rollups.
chat: usage_events table (tokens per request) with hourly continuous aggregates for billing dashboards.
notes: LICENSE quote: 'Outside of the "tsl" directory, source code ... is licensed under the Apache License Version 2.0' and 'Within the "tsl" folder, source code ... is licensed under the Timescale License'. Editions doc: Apache 2 edition can be sold as a service; 'You cannot sell TimescaleDB Community Edition as a service.' Community-only features include Hypercore columnstore, continuous aggregates, retention policies, jobs. licence_class set to source_available because the commonly used feature set is TSL; the Apache-only build is permissive. Rename quote (2025-06-17): 'TimescaleDB is now Tiger Data.' and 'Our open source time-series PostgreSQL extension remains TimescaleDB.' 2018 and 2020 TSL dates come from a 2024-03-13 Tiger Data post ('Back in 2018, Timescale first announced...'; 'updated our license in 2020'); exact days unconfirmed (original posts not reached). Multi-node: CHANGELOG 2.14.0 (2024-02-08): 'Multi-node is no longer supported starting with TimescaleDB 2.14.' Tiering to object storage is a Tiger Cloud feature (from memory of docs, not re-fetched). Which other cloud Postgres services ship only the Apache edition: not confirmed this session. No Jepsen analysis.
